_about: Written moat assessments by Claude in chat (spec 2026-11-13). rating W 1-9 on the rubric: 9 near-monopoly, decades; 8 one overwhelming source + supporting, clear leader; 7 strong source, leader, 10+ yrs; 6 real but narrow/contestable; 5 some advantage, not decisive; 4 weak, easily copied; 3 wasting (patent cliff, technology shift) or fragile; 2 no advantage, model is a liability; 1 anti-moat. sources = Morningstar's five (0 none, 1 some, 2 strong); why = the source(s); durability = how long it lasts; invalidation = what would break it. No assessment is published without all three. Final = min(round(0.6W + 0.4C), W + 1). Loaded into scr_moat_review with scripts/load-moat-reviews.mjs.

ALGM.why: Leader in magnetic sensors for cars; parts are designed into vehicle platforms for years, but chips are cyclical and several rivals compete.
ALGM.invalidation: Rivals' sensors win the next car platforms, or the auto chip cycle stays weak for years

AMZN.why: AWS is hard to leave once a company is built on it; the marketplace grows stronger as buyers and sellers attract each other; its delivery network is too costly for most to copy.
AMZN.invalidation: AWS loses its lead to Microsoft/Google or regulators force a break-up of retail and marketplace

ASML.why: The only maker of EUV lithography machines, which every leading-edge chip needs; decades of know-how and a supplier chain no one else has.
ASML.invalidation: A rival (Chinese or Japanese) builds a working EUV machine, or chipmaking moves to a different method

AVGO.why: Leads in networking chips and custom AI chips designed with each customer; VMware software is deeply embedded in company data centres.
AVGO.invalidation: Hyperscalers design networking and AI chips fully in-house, or VMware customers leave over pricing

AXON.why: Taser plus body cameras plus evidence cloud sold together to police forces; once a department's records live in Axon's system, switching is slow and costly.
AXON.invalidation: A rival bundles body cameras and evidence software cheaper and police budgets or rules shift

BWXT.why: Sole supplier of nuclear reactors for US Navy submarines and carriers; government licences and security clearances make it practically irreplaceable.
BWXT.invalidation: The US Navy changes reactor suppliers or naval nuclear programs are cut sharply

CAT.why: Strongest brand in heavy machinery with the largest dealer and service network; results swing with construction and mining cycles.
CAT.invalidation: Chinese makers win on price globally, or electric machinery resets the dealer and service advantage

FTNT.why: Firewalls built on its own chips give it a price-performance edge, and customers rarely rip out security gear; the market has many strong rivals.
FTNT.invalidation: Security moves fully to cloud services where its own chips matter less

GD.why: One of only two US nuclear submarine builders and a top business-jet maker (Gulfstream); profits are steady but margins are modest.
GD.invalidation: Submarine programs are cut or Gulfstream loses the top end of business jets

GEV.why: One of three makers of large gas turbines, with a huge installed base that pays for decades of service; wind business has been a drag on the numbers.
GEV.invalidation: Gas turbine demand fades as grids switch to batteries/renewables, or service contracts reprice

GOOG.why: Search, YouTube and Android each dominate their market; more users improve the products and the ads; AI chatbots are the main threat.
GOOG.invalidation: AI assistants replace search as the way people find things and ads follow them elsewhere

HONA.why: Engines, cockpit systems and parts certified onto aircraft for their whole life; airlines must buy spare parts and service from it for decades.
HONA.invalidation: Aircraft makers move parts in-house or certification rules loosen for rival parts

KLAC.why: More than half of the market for chip inspection and measurement tools; its data is built into every leading chip factory's process.
KLAC.invalidation: Applied Materials or a new entrant matches its inspection data at leading-edge fabs

LLY.why: Patents on leading weight-loss and diabetes drugs plus scarce large-scale manufacturing; patents expire and rivals are racing to catch up.
LLY.invalidation: Rivals' weight-loss drugs match it at lower prices, or key patents fall in the mid-2030s

LRCX.why: Leader in etching equipment, critical for memory chips; tools are designed into chip factories, but spending is cyclical.
LRCX.invalidation: Memory spending collapses for years or rivals win etching at new chip designs

MCD.why: World's best-known restaurant brand; owns the land under many franchised restaurants and collects rent and fees regardless of food trends.
MCD.invalidation: Franchisees rebel or the brand loses relevance with younger customers

META.why: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp have billions of users who stay because their friends are there; advertisers follow the users.
META.invalidation: Users and attention move to a rival platform (as with TikTok) or rules restrict targeted ads

MSFT.why: Windows, Office and Azure are built into how most companies work; files, logins and staff skills make leaving very costly.
MSFT.invalidation: Businesses move core work to AI-native rivals or Google Workspace wins enterprises

NFLX.why: Biggest streaming service, so it can spend more on shows per subscriber than rivals; but viewers can cancel any month.
NFLX.invalidation: Rival streamers outspend it on content, or growth stalls and pricing power fades

NOC.why: Sole builder of the B-21 bomber and the Sentinel missile; decades-long government programmes with few possible competitors.
NOC.invalidation: B-21 or Sentinel programs are cancelled or cut back

NOW.why: Runs IT and workflow processes inside large companies; once processes are built on it, switching takes years.
NOW.invalidation: AI agents let companies run workflows without a central platform

NVDA.why: CUDA software that millions of developers use locks AI work to its chips; big customers are designing their own chips to reduce dependence.
NVDA.invalidation: Custom chips (Google TPU, Amazon, AMD) break the CUDA lock-in for AI workloads

SNOW.why: Data stored and shared on Snowflake is sticky, but strong rivals (Databricks, the big clouds) compete on price and it still loses money.
SNOW.invalidation: Databricks or the cloud providers take the data-platform market on price

SNPS.why: One of two companies whose software every chip designer needs; engineers are trained on its tools and chip designs depend on them.
SNPS.invalidation: AI-native design tools from a new rival, or export controls cut its China business deeply

SOLS.why: Patents on low-emission refrigerants that regulations push customers toward; chemicals face competition when patents age.
SOLS.invalidation: Refrigerant patents expire or rules change to favour other cooling chemicals

SPCX.why: Reusable rockets make its launches far cheaper than rivals'; Starlink has more satellites in orbit than everyone else combined.
SPCX.invalidation: Rivals match reusable rockets (Blue Origin, China) or Starlink faces strong satellite competition

SPGI.why: One of two dominant credit-rating agencies and owner of the S&P 500 index; bond issuers and fund managers effectively must use it.
SPGI.invalidation: Regulators change how ratings are required, or index investing moves to cheaper benchmarks

TDG.why: Sole-source certified aircraft parts; airlines can't swap suppliers, so it can raise prices on spares. Carries a lot of debt.
TDG.invalidation: Airlines and regulators force cheaper replacement parts, or debt becomes a problem in a downturn

TER.why: One of two main makers of chip testing machines; demand is cyclical and the robotics unit has been weak.
TER.invalidation: Advantest takes its share of chip testing, or robotics keeps losing money

TMO.why: Largest supplier of lab equipment and consumables; its products are written into drug-making processes approved by regulators, so they rarely change.
TMO.invalidation: Drug makers move to cheaper suppliers or bring lab products in-house

TSM.why: Makes nearly all of the world's most advanced chips; rivals are years behind and a new factory costs tens of billions. Taiwan location is a risk.
TSM.invalidation: Intel or Samsung catch up at the leading edge, or a Taiwan conflict disrupts production

V.why: Largest card network: shops accept it because shoppers carry it and the reverse; a duopoly with Mastercard.
V.invalidation: Real-time bank payments or stablecoins bypass card networks, or regulators cap fees

VEEV.why: Standard software for drug companies' sales and clinical trials; regulated data and validated processes make switching slow.
VEEV.invalidation: Salesforce or AI tools win drug companies' sales and clinical software

WMT.why: Scale gives it the lowest costs in retail and buying power over suppliers; growing ads and marketplace businesses.
WMT.invalidation: Amazon wins on price and delivery, or margins fall in a price war

AAPL.why: iPhone users are tied in by apps, photos and other Apple devices; the App Store earns on every developer's sales.
AAPL.invalidation: A new device replaces the smartphone, or rules force open the App Store and its fees

TSLA.why: Strong brand and charging network, but car makers compete on price and Chinese rivals are catching up.
TSLA.invalidation: Chinese and legacy carmakers match its cars and software at lower prices

BRK-A.why: Insurance float invested by a disciplined owner, plus a wide set of businesses (BNSF railway, utilities) that are hard to copy.
BRK-A.invalidation: Capital allocation weakens after its founders, or a major insurance loss

BRK-B.why: Insurance float invested by a disciplined owner, plus a wide set of businesses (BNSF railway, utilities) that are hard to copy.
BRK-B.invalidation: Capital allocation weakens after its founders, or a major insurance loss

SKHY.why: One of three memory chip makers and leader in AI high-bandwidth memory; memory prices swing hard with the cycle.
SKHY.invalidation: Samsung and Micron catch up in high-bandwidth memory, or AI chip demand falls

AMD.why: Strong chip designs in servers and PCs, but competes head-on with Intel and NVIDIA, whose software ecosystem is deeper.
AMD.invalidation: NVIDIA and Intel out-execute it, or customers' own chips take its share

JPM.why: Largest US bank with low-cost deposits and leading investment bank; scale spreads technology and compliance costs.
JPM.invalidation: A major credit loss or tech-led rivals take deposits and payments

MU.why: One of three memory chip makers; products are largely interchangeable, so profits follow the boom-bust memory cycle.
MU.invalidation: Memory prices crash again, as they do every few years

XOM.why: Low-cost oil fields and integrated refining give it an edge, but it sells a commodity at whatever oil fetches.
XOM.invalidation: Oil demand falls structurally or prices stay low for years

JNJ.why: Patented drugs plus surgical and heart devices that surgeons are trained on; drugs lose protection as patents expire.
JNJ.invalidation: Patent losses on big drugs without replacements, or major legal liabilities

MA.why: Second-largest card network: shops accept it because shoppers carry it and the reverse; a duopoly with Visa.
MA.invalidation: Real-time bank payments or stablecoins bypass card networks, or regulators cap fees

ABBV.why: Patented immunology drugs (Skyrizi, Rinvoq) replacing Humira; each drug's protection ends with its patents.
ABBV.invalidation: Skyrizi and Rinvoq lose share to rivals, or patents end in the 2030s

COST.why: Membership fees and huge volume let it sell at near-cost prices no rival matches; members renew over 90% of the time.
COST.invalidation: Members stop renewing, or online rivals match its prices

CVX.why: Low-cost oil fields and refining; sells a commodity, so profits follow oil prices.
CVX.invalidation: Oil demand falls structurally or prices stay low for years

KO.why: The world's best-known drink brand with bottlers in nearly every country; shelf space and habit are hard to dislodge.
KO.invalidation: Tastes move away from sugary drinks faster than it can adapt its brands

CSCO.why: Network gear is built into most company networks and staff are trained on it; cloud and rivals have eroded the edge.
CSCO.invalidation: Cloud and white-box networking keep taking share from its gear

PLTR.why: Software deeply built into government and company decisions; hard to remove, but expensive and faced by many AI rivals.
PLTR.invalidation: Government contracts shift to cheaper AI tools, or commercial growth stalls

PG.why: Leading brands (Tide, Pampers, Gillette) and scale in advertising and distribution; store brands push on price.
PG.invalidation: Store brands and online rivals win on price

ORCL.why: Its databases run the core systems of most big companies and are very costly to move; cloud business growing fast with heavy spending.
ORCL.invalidation: Customers move databases to cloud-native rivals, or AI data-centre spending fails to pay back

UNH.why: Largest health insurer plus Optum's doctors and data; scale lowers costs, but regulation and rising medical costs pressure it.
UNH.invalidation: Regulators restrict its insurance/Optum combination, or medical costs keep outrunning prices

MRK.why: Patented drugs and vaccines; Keytruda, its biggest seller, loses US patent protection around 2028.
MRK.invalidation: Keytruda's US patent expires around 2028 without enough new drugs to replace it

BAC.why: Huge low-cost deposit base and scale in consumer banking; earnings follow interest rates and the economy.
BAC.invalidation: A major credit loss or tech-led rivals take deposits

HD.why: Largest home-improvement chain with buying power and the best service to contractors; one of two national players.
HD.invalidation: Online sellers win contractors, or a long housing slump

GE.why: Its jet engines are on most new airliners and must be serviced by GE for decades; one of very few engine makers.
GE.invalidation: Engine reliability problems, or rivals win the next generation of airliners

INTC.why: Still the largest PC chip seller, but lost its manufacturing lead and is spending heavily to catch up.
INTC.invalidation: Its chipmaking turnaround fails and customers stay with TSMC

PM.why: Marlboro abroad and IQOS heated tobacco, protected by addiction and strict rules on advertising for new entrants.
PM.invalidation: Heated tobacco and nicotine pouches face bans, or smoking declines faster

HSBC.why: Large global bank strong in Asian trade finance; banks compete on rates and are tied to the economy.
HSBC.invalidation: China/Hong Kong slowdown or new competition in trade finance

NVS.why: Patented medicines across heart, cancer and immunology; each drug's advantage ends with its patents.
NVS.invalidation: Key drugs lose patents without new ones to replace them

AMAT.why: Largest maker of chip equipment with the broadest range of tools; demand is cyclical.
AMAT.invalidation: Chip spending falls for years or export controls cut China sales deeply

MS.why: Leading wealth manager and investment bank; client assets are sticky, trading profits swing with markets.
MS.invalidation: Market slump hits trading and wealth fees, or rivals undercut advice fees

AZN.why: Patented cancer and rare-disease drugs with a strong pipeline; protection ends with each patent.
AZN.invalidation: Key cancer drugs lose patents without replacements

TXN.why: Tens of thousands of analog chips designed into products for decades; owns its own low-cost factories.
TXN.invalidation: Chinese analog makers win on price, or its factory spending fails to pay back

RY.why: Canada's largest bank in a market dominated by a handful of banks; strong deposit base.
RY.invalidation: Canadian banking rules open the market, or a housing crash hits loans

SHEL.why: Large oil, gas and LNG trading business; sells commodities, so profits follow prices.
SHEL.invalidation: Oil and gas demand falls structurally or prices stay low

SAP.why: Runs the core finance and operations systems of most big companies; switching takes years and huge sums.
SAP.invalidation: Cloud-native or AI rivals replace its core systems at large companies

RTX.why: Pratt engines and Collins parts are certified on aircraft and need decades of service; engine problems have cost billions.
RTX.invalidation: Engine problems continue, or defence budgets shrink

PANW.why: Broadest set of security products; companies that use several of them find it hard to move away.
PANW.invalidation: Rivals' platforms (Microsoft, CrowdStrike) win the security bundle

GS.why: Top investment bank brand and relationships; results swing with markets and deal activity.
GS.invalidation: Deal activity stays low, or regulation squeezes trading

ANET.why: Network switches running AI and cloud data centres with its own software; heavily reliant on a few big customers.
ANET.invalidation: Its biggest cloud customers move to in-house or NVIDIA networking

WFC.why: Large US deposit base and branch network; still recovering from years of regulatory restrictions.
WFC.invalidation: A major credit loss or tech-led rivals take deposits

AMGN.why: Biotech with patented drugs and manufacturing know-how for complex biologics; faces biosimilar copies.
AMGN.invalidation: Biosimilars erode its older drugs faster than new ones grow

TM.why: Toyota's lean manufacturing and reliability brand give it a cost and quality edge; car making is intensely competitive.
TM.invalidation: Electric-car rivals win on cost and software

MUFG.why: Japan's largest bank; low-cost deposits but a mature, low-margin market.
MUFG.invalidation: Japanese rates stay low or competition from digital banks

LIN.why: Industrial gases piped to customers on long contracts; plants are local monopolies with few rivals.
LIN.invalidation: Industrial demand falls sharply or customers build their own gas plants

DELL.why: Scale in PCs and servers with low costs; products are largely interchangeable with rivals'.
DELL.invalidation: PC and server prices fall; AI server margins stay thin

CRWD.why: Security software that learns from every customer's data; once installed on all devices, switching is a big project.
CRWD.invalidation: Microsoft's bundled security wins, or another major outage costs trust

BABA.why: Taobao and Tmall marketplace plus China's top cloud; heavy competition from PDD and Douyin, and regulation risk.
BABA.invalidation: PDD and Douyin keep taking share, or Chinese regulation tightens again

IBM.why: Mainframes and consulting embedded in large companies; slow growth as clients move to newer clouds.
IBM.invalidation: Mainframe users move to cloud and consulting loses work to AI

ARM.why: Chip designs used in nearly every phone; the software world is built for its instruction set.
ARM.invalidation: RISC-V (an open, free alternative) takes phones and data centres

AXP.why: Premium brand with wealthy cardholders who spend more; runs its own network, so earns from both sides.
AXP.invalidation: Premium cards lose appeal or regulators cap fees

TD.why: One of Canada's big banks, plus a large US branch network; strong deposits, but US money-laundering penalties.
TD.invalidation: US money-laundering penalties keep limiting its US growth

GILD.why: Leader in HIV medicines that patients stay on for life; patents eventually expire.
GILD.invalidation: HIV drugs lose patents around 2030s without replacements

C.why: Global bank strongest in corporate cash services; lower returns than peers, mid-turnaround.
C.invalidation: Its restructuring fails and returns stay below peers

BHP.why: Owns some of the world's lowest-cost iron ore and copper mines; prices are set by the market.
BHP.invalidation: Iron ore demand falls as China builds less

DIS.why: Unmatched characters and theme parks; TV channels are shrinking and streaming is crowded.
DIS.invalidation: Theme parks slow and streaming never earns enough to replace TV

TTE.why: Integrated oil and gas plus LNG and power; sells commodities, so profits follow prices.
TTE.invalidation: Oil and gas demand falls structurally or prices stay low

ADI.why: Analog and power chips designed into industrial and car products for many years; high margins.
ADI.invalidation: Chinese analog makers win on price in industrial and car markets

APH.why: Connectors and cables designed into devices; huge product range and decentralised management keep costs low.
APH.invalidation: Customers standardise connectors and buy on price

PEP.why: Frito-Lay snacks and Pepsi drinks with direct-store delivery that few rivals can match.
PEP.invalidation: Snack and soda demand falls with health trends and weight-loss drugs

VZ.why: One of three US mobile networks; heavy spending and price competition limit returns.
VZ.invalidation: Price war with T-Mobile/AT&T or cable companies' mobile offers

QCOM.why: Patents every phone maker licenses and leading phone chips; Apple is replacing its modems.
QCOM.invalidation: Apple and others replace its modems with their own chips

SHOP.why: Online store software for millions of merchants; apps, payments and data make switching painful.
SHOP.invalidation: Amazon or social platforms take merchants, or AI shopping agents bypass its stores

BLK.why: Largest asset manager with iShares ETFs and the Aladdin system used by other investors; scale lowers fees.
BLK.invalidation: Fee cuts squeeze returns, or a rival wins the ETF price war

ABT.why: Glucose monitors, heart devices and diagnostics that doctors trust; broad and steady.
ABT.invalidation: Rivals' glucose monitors win on price, or device recalls

DE.why: Leading farm equipment brand with the best dealer network and precision-farming software; cyclical.
DE.invalidation: Farm incomes fall for years, or rivals' autonomy software wins

TMUS.why: One of three US mobile networks with the strongest 5G network; competition limits pricing power.
TMUS.invalidation: Price war with Verizon/AT&T or cable companies' mobile offers

UNP.why: Owns a western US rail network that can't be duplicated; one of two railways in the region.
UNP.invalidation: Freight moves to trucks (autonomous trucking) or regulators impose open access

WELL.why: Owns senior housing and medical buildings; benefits from ageing population, but property is competitive.
WELL.invalidation: Senior housing oversupply or operator failures

NVO.why: Pioneer of GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic, Wegovy) but losing share to Lilly and facing generics outside the US.
NVO.invalidation: Lilly and generics take weight-loss share, semaglutide patents end early 2030s

CRM.why: Sales and service software at the heart of many companies; data and workflows make switching slow.
CRM.invalidation: AI agents or Microsoft take its sales and service software

NEE.why: Florida's regulated utility plus the largest renewable developer; scale lowers costs.
NEE.invalidation: Florida regulation turns against it, or renewables lose subsidies

SAN.why: Large bank across Spain, UK and Latin America; banks compete on rates.
SAN.invalidation: Latin American downturns or a UK/Spain housing crisis

COP.why: Largest independent oil producer with low-cost US shale; profits follow oil prices.
COP.invalidation: Oil demand falls structurally or prices stay low

BUD.why: Owns the top beer brands and distribution in many countries; beer volumes are flat.
BUD.invalidation: Beer volumes fall faster as drinking habits change

PFE.why: Large drug maker facing many patent expiries this decade; rebuilding with acquisitions.
PFE.invalidation: Several big drugs lose patents by 2028 without enough replacements

DHR.why: Bioprocessing and lab tools built into approved drug-making processes; switching needs regulator sign-off.
DHR.invalidation: Drug makers change suppliers in new processes, or biotech funding stays weak

SONY.why: PlayStation's network of players and image-sensor leadership; music and film catalogues.
SONY.invalidation: PlayStation loses its lead, or image sensors lose to Samsung

SCHW.why: Huge low-cost brokerage where client assets rarely move; earns on clients' cash.
SCHW.invalidation: Clients move cash to higher-yield accounts, or fee price war

ISRG.why: Da Vinci surgical robots: surgeons train for years on them and hospitals buy instruments for each operation.
ISRG.invalidation: Rival surgical robots (Medtronic, J&J) win hospitals on price

TJX.why: Buys brand-name surplus stock cheaply and sells it at a discount; buying network is hard to copy.
TJX.invalidation: Brands sell more surplus online directly, cutting off its supply

T.why: One of three US mobile networks plus fibre; high debt and price competition.
T.invalidation: Price war in mobile, or fibre rivals in home internet

UBS.why: World's largest wealth manager; client money is sticky, but integrating Credit Suisse.
UBS.invalidation: Credit Suisse integration problems or Swiss capital rules squeeze returns

ACN.why: Largest consulting and IT services firm; long client relationships, but AI may reduce billable work.
ACN.invalidation: AI cuts the need for consultants and IT outsourcing

MRVL.why: Custom AI chips and networking chips for data centres; depends on a few large customers.
MRVL.invalidation: Its few big cloud customers switch suppliers or design chips themselves

BBVA.why: Strong in Spain and Mexico with good digital banking; banks compete on rates.

SCCO.why: Owns the world's largest copper reserves with low costs; copper price drives profits.
SCCO.invalidation: Copper prices fall for years, or Peru/Mexico political risk

IBKR.why: Highly automated broker with the lowest costs in the industry; earns on client cash.
IBKR.invalidation: Rivals match its low costs, or a trading loss in volatile markets

UL.why: Global consumer brands (Dove, Hellmann's) with strong reach in emerging markets.
UL.invalidation: Store brands and local rivals take share in emerging markets

CB.why: Global insurer with strict underwriting discipline; insurance is competitive but Chubb prices well.
CB.invalidation: Catastrophe losses or a softer insurance market cut its pricing

UBER.why: Largest ride and delivery network: more drivers mean shorter waits and more riders; robotaxis are a threat.

LMT.why: Builds the F-35 and missiles under long government contracts; few competitors can bid.
LMT.invalidation: F-35 orders are cut or rivals win the next fighter programs

ETN.why: Electrical equipment for data centres and buildings; reliable brand, but competitive industry.
ETN.invalidation: Electrical demand from data centres slows, rivals win on price

VRTX.why: Near-monopoly in cystic fibrosis medicines; patents protect it for years.
VRTX.invalidation: New cystic-fibrosis rivals, or patents end in the late 2030s

BX.why: Largest alternative asset manager; investors lock money in for years and its brand attracts new funds.
BX.invalidation: Property losses or investors pull money from private funds

PGR.why: Leader in pricing car insurance with data; lower costs than most rivals.
PGR.invalidation: Rivals' data and pricing catch up, or car-insurance price wars

BA.why: One of two makers of large airliners; production problems and debt have hurt it badly.
BA.invalidation: Safety and production problems continue and Airbus keeps taking orders

RIO.why: Owns some of the world's lowest-cost iron ore mines; commodity prices drive profits.
RIO.invalidation: Iron ore demand falls as China builds less

SNDK.why: Flash memory maker; products compete on price in a boom-bust market.

HDB.why: India's largest private bank with low-cost deposits and strong growth.
HDB.invalidation: Indian bank competition or a credit downturn

BTI.why: Global tobacco brands protected by addiction and advertising limits; smoking volumes are falling.
BTI.invalidation: Smoking falls faster, or new nicotine products are banned

MO.why: Marlboro in the US; addiction and advertising limits protect it, but smoking is declining.
MO.invalidation: Smoking falls faster, or new nicotine products are banned

MDT.why: Heart and surgical devices that doctors are trained on; slow growth.
MDT.invalidation: Rivals take share in heart and surgical devices

LOW.why: Second of two national home-improvement chains; buying power and store network.
LOW.invalidation: Long housing slump, or Home Depot widens its lead with contractors

BMY.why: Patented drugs, but its biggest sellers face patent expiry soon.
BMY.invalidation: Eliquis and Opdivo lose patents around 2028 without enough replacements

STX.why: One of two hard-drive makers for data centres; cyclical demand.
STX.invalidation: Flash storage replaces hard drives in data centres

MCK.why: One of three US drug wholesalers; huge volumes on thin margins.
MCK.invalidation: A big pharmacy customer leaves, or drug-pricing rules squeeze margins

IBN.why: One of India's largest private banks with low-cost deposits.
IBN.invalidation: Indian bank competition or a credit downturn

SPOT.why: Largest music streaming service; playlists and habits keep users, but pays most revenue to labels.
SPOT.invalidation: Labels raise royalties or Apple/YouTube outcompete it

MFG.why: Large Japanese bank; mature, low-margin market.
MFG.invalidation: Japanese rates stay low or digital competition

SBUX.why: Strong coffee brand and loyalty app; competition and costs have hurt recent results.

PLD.why: Largest owner of warehouses near big cities, where land is scarce.

ADP.why: Payroll for a large share of US employers; switching payroll is risky, so clients stay for years.

PH.why: Motion-control parts designed into machines and aircraft; large spare-parts business.

BMO.why: One of Canada's big banks, with a US arm; deposit base.

BP.why: Oil and gas major; strategy shifts and debt weigh on returns.
BP.invalidation: Strategy shifts and debt weigh on returns, or oil prices fall

BKNG.why: Largest online hotel booking site: hotels list where travellers search and the reverse.
BKNG.invalidation: Google or AI travel agents take bookings directly

SYK.why: Orthopaedic implants and robots that surgeons train on; hospitals stay with the system.
SYK.invalidation: Rival robots and implants win surgeons

APP.why: Ad technology that uses data from many apps; very profitable, but competition and platform rules can change.

NEM.why: Largest gold miner; gold price drives profits.

PBR.why: Low-cost deep-water oil fields; government influence on pricing and spending.

WDC.why: One of two hard-drive makers; cyclical.
